- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to catch upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >+3% from model, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, model likely overreacted; reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to correct; add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.4 within next 3 days.
